1.why: Two sound options (D finding+prior-research, B finding+caveat); D reads as the plain full result and A is its overreach twin, but B subsumes C the same way, so this is a coin flip I resolved by family-cast.

2.why: A, B and D are three single dated stages; C is the only option that generalizes over all of them and adds the endpoint.

3.why: A, B and C are isolated facts; D is the only causally complete sentence and it subsumes their content.

4.why: C is the only option carrying who/when/how-many/why while A, B and D are one-clause findings, but A could equally be the conclusion the other two build to.

5.why: B is the only option holding two elements in tension (self-rated alertness vs 24-hour-awake reaction times); A, C, D are single fragments of it.

6.why: A, C and D are the three components of the design; B is the only one that states what the pair of experiments together established.

7.why: Four different rhetorical acts with no stem to choose between them; B states the finding and then restates its magnitude, the shape keys take when the goal is emphasis.

8.why: C is D plus the result, so it subsumes another option outright, but A is an equally complete causal sentence and I cannot rule it out.

9.why: C is the explicit both-numbers comparison that A and B each supply half of; D drops the figures entirely.

10.why: B contains all of A plus an evaluation of it, but C is the bare finding and would be the key under a different goal.

11.why: D is the only option that generalizes across the studies; A contradicts the others and B, C are single parameters.

12.why: B is the only option pairing the measured outcome with its figure (3 kg / eight weeks); D is its vague twin and C the caveat family.

13.why: D is the mechanism; C is visibly defective ('must be ... every structure the Romans ever built') and A, B are partial.

14.why: B is the convergence statement over three methods; A, C, D are single figures, one of which (A) is a member of B's own set.

15.why: C is the causal chain linking hippocampus, BDNF and memory scores, but B is also multi-element (consistency across ages) and would win a different goal.

16.why: D states the full otter-urchin-kelp chain and both directions of it; A, B, C are each one link of D.

17.why: No option synthesizes the others here - four parallel facts; B is picked only because it carries the casualty figure and the stakes clause, which is weak.

18.why: Two distinct limitation options (C duration, D sample); D hedges the finding explicitly, but nothing in the set decides between them.

19.why: A holds the fluctuation and the long-term decline together with both endpoints; D asserts the opposite direction and B, C are single facts.

20.why: A generalizes across 11 of 12 vents and three oceans, but C (role in the food web) is an equally complete standalone claim.

21.why: Held my directional rule and took the full finding across 100 cities, though A (correlation-not-causation) is the option I would pick if the goal were to qualify.

22.why: A is the only complete causal mechanism (weathering releases minerals, hence fertility); C merely juxtaposes the same two facts.

23.why: D is the explicit acceleration comparison (2.5 km vs 0.4 km) that the other three options each supply one side or the method of.

24.why: B names one cause driving all three changes that A, C and D pair off two at a time.
